content:
"I miss you. What are you up to?"

I don't know who to send this to. I’ll just leave it here.

Have I become the person I once despised, living off hollow intimacy? I’ve grown used to having someone—beside me or in my phone. It doesn't really matter who. I just need that silent belief that someone loves me, that someone "got my back." Eventually, I grow tired, annoyed. I watch her cry until her tears run dry, then I replace her with someone new, feeling absolutely nothing. All those blurred lines and ambiguities... perhaps they are just the shadows of "youth." Dark, yet structured, they are the evidence of my existence on the canvas—the inevitable result of being exposed to the sun. Or so I tell myself to ease the guilt.

I used to be so insecure. I witnessed couples blooming all around me; I watched my friends walk away and into the arms of others, leaving me behind. I blessed them from the bottom of my heart, yet I screamed from the depths of it, too. I craved validation so much. I was so desperate for tenderness. I just wanted someone to hold me and tell me, "Everything is going to be okay." To treat me like a child, or an infant. If I could return to the womb, that would be even better. Maybe my mother had her own troubles back then, or perhaps she simply lacked the power to stuff me back in and start over.

Is being liked the only form of self-affirmation? I refuse to believe that. So, I slapped my younger self across the face. He became even more insecure.

For someone with such fierce pride, I never resisted dressing as a girl. Staring at that stranger in the mirror, I’d sigh—that kind of girl would never love me, but I could briefly become her. But when I take off the wig and the skirt, she doesn’t leave. She made me fall in love with a concept, an image, a perfect "Me." So maybe, there was never room for anyone else in my heart. There is only me, and Me.

"What are we now?" I have no answer. Am I afraid of a predetermined future? Promises I can't keep? Or is it that I simply don't love you as much as I love myself? Of course I love you, but I just love everyone equally... right? Or do I just want to be loved by everyone equally, so I can squander it as I please.

Through all these years of drifting, the only skill I’ve truly mastered is "not giving a damn." I never learned how to meet or embrace; I only learned how to say goodbye. I know I’m pushing a boulder. I know it will eventually roll back down. I know this is my punishment.

Tell me, Mr. Camus—am I happy?
title: Exhausted
